title: Living off the VPN — Exploring VPN Post-Exploitation Techniques

scenario.summary: Hardcoded Secrets / Credential Exposure writeup against Ivanti (Connect Secure), Fortinet (Fortigate VPN).
preconditions: A secret (API key, password, private key) is embedded in client-side code, a public repository, or a publicly accessible file

process.action: Search client-side JavaScript bundles, mobile app binaries, and public repositories for secret-like strings
process.expected_observation: Candidate strings matching API key/token/private-key formats found

process.action: Validate whether the discovered secret is live and what scope/permissions it grants
tools: provider's API (e.g. test call with the key)
process.expected_observation: Key authenticates successfully and reveals its permission scope

process.action: Determine the blast radius of the credential (which systems/data it can access)
process.expected_observation: List of resources/actions accessible with the leaked credential

impact: Unauthorized access to the associated third-party service or internal system
Potential for lateral movement or data exfiltration depending on credential scope
remediation: Never embed secrets in client-distributed code or commit them to version control
Use short-lived, scoped tokens issued per-session from a backend, not long-lived static keys
Add automated secret scanning to CI/CD and rotate any credential that is ever exposed
